newsitem.title: GERMANY: Denmark's Tivoli to license Berlin theme park plan.
newsitem.headline: Denmark's Tivoli to license Berlin theme park plan.

text.p: A German company said on Tuesday it planned to sign a licensing deal in March with Denmark's Tivoli International to design an amusement park in Berlin modelled on Copenhagen's famous Tivoli Gardens.

The deal will be signed on March 7 with Tivoli-Berlin, a newly-founded local firm, to draft plans for a park stretching from the capital into neighbouring Brandenburg which would then be submitted to the capital's planning authorities.

A spokesman for Tivoli-Berlin said the 30 hectare (75 acre) park, whose estimated cost would be between 500 and 700 million marks ($300 to $400 million) would feature three hotels, concert halls, theatres, rides, restaurants and gardens.

"The deal centres on the introductory phases of working out a master plan to set up an amusement park in Berlin-Brandenburg following the Tivoli Gardens concept," Tivoli International said in a statement released in Copenhagen on Monday.
"If the amusement park is set up, Tivoli International will provide know-how and assistance along lines to be agreed at a later stage," the statement added.
Tivoli-Berlin, a consortium of German brewers and food industry firms, plans to start building in early 1998.
The Danish company said it did not plan to offer capital or direct management assistance for the park, which is scheduled for completion in the year 2000.
The Tivoli-Berlin spokesman said he expected the project to create over 4,000 jobs for the unemployment-hit Berlin-Brandenburg region.
